newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt says Democrats have learned lessons.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt says Democrats have learned lessons.

text.p: House of Representatives Minority Leader Richard Gephardt said that the Democratic Party has learned the lessons of its 1994 defeat and would curb its liberal instincts if Democrats are restored to power.

In an interview in Monday's Washington Post, the Missouri Democrat said Democrats were poised to win back the House and would return with a more modest agenda than they had two years ago when they lost control of the legislature.
"What we're saying to people is, we are a better product. We will do a better job," the Post quoted Gephardt as saying.

Gephardt, asked whether House Democrats concluded their previous agenda was too liberal, replied, "They realise that we did not produce what the American people wanted ... I've said many times, we're all 'new Democrats' now ... we have to be. Times change."
Gephardt pointed to the Democrat's new "Families First" agenda as a sign of more modest ambitions of the congressional wing of the party, the Post reported.

"We had 120 ideas that these members came in with for the agenda. Most of them were rejected," the paper quoted him as saying. "This is what we're going to do. They may be a lot of other things that individual members would like to do. This is what the team is going to do."
The Democratic agenda calls for targeted tax breaks for child care and education, balancing the budget without deep cuts in Medicare, and other centrist-sounding proposals.

In the first two years of President Clinton's term, when Democrats still controlled the House, they helped load up the crime bill with billions in new spending which Republicans described as a pork-barrel giveaways.
Gephardt said Democrats poised to take over control of key House committees if the party wins control again agreed on the need for a more modest agenda.
He also stressed the need for bipartisan votes on key issues and said he would work hard to get Republican support if he becomes Speaker of the House.
